tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in clean, transparent watch glass or glass dish to detect any foreign particles, conformance of colour & compliance with the visual specifications.
Mix small quantity of sample with water. Note full miscibility with water. It may partly or totally solidify at room temperature and liquefies again when heated to 50 °C.

Visual examination: It is a clear, colorless or brown, viscous liquid, miscible with water. The substance may partly or totally solidify at room temperature and liquefies again when heated to 50 °C. Specification: It is a clear, syrupy liquid at 25 °C.
Dissolve 0.1 g in 2.5 mL of water. Heat with 2.5 mL of cupri-tartaric solution. A red precipitate is formed.

Dip, for 1 s, a suitable stick with a reactive pad containing glucose-oxidase, peroxidase and a hydrogen-donating substance, such as tetramethylbenzidine, in a 5 g/L solution of the substance to be examined. Observe the color of the reactive pad; within 60 s the color changes from yellow to green or blue.
Mix 1 mL of a 223.6 g/L solution of potassium chloride and 30 mL of solution S (25.0 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL). Measure using a calibrated pH meter.

details.solutionS: 25.0 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL
details.kclSolution: 1 mL of 223.6 g/L KCl solution with 30 mL Solution S
details.reference: BP Appendix V L. Determination of pH Values; BP 2025 Monograph for Liquid Glucose

tests.procedure: Accurately weigh empty crucible previously ignited at 600-650 °C (W0). Weigh 1.0 g into crucible (W1). Moisten with ~1 mL sulfuric acid, heat gently on hot plate until thoroughly charred. Cool, moisten again with sulfuric acid, heat until white fumes cease. Ignite in muffle at 600-650 °C, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2). Repeat to constant weight. % Sulfated ash = (W2 - W0) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: BP Appendix IX A. Determination of Sulfated Ash; BP 2025 Monograph for Liquid Glucose

tests.procedure: Accurately weigh empty weighing bottle previously dried at 80 °C (W0). Weigh accurately 1.000 g into weighing bottle (W1). Dry in calibrated oven at 80 °C for 2 h. Cool in desiccator, weigh (W2). Repeat to constant weight. % Loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.formula: % Loss on Drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100
details.reference: BP Appendix IX D. Determination of Loss on Drying; BP 2025 Monograph for Liquid Glucose

tests.procedure: Introduce 150 mL water into flask A, pass CO2 for 15 min at 100 ± 5 mL/min. To 10 mL dilute H2O2 add 0.15 mL 1 g/L bromophenol blue in ethanol (20% V/V), add 0.1 M NaOH until violet-blue colour obtained without exceeding endpoint. Place in tube D. Add 25.0 g sample with 100 mL water to flask A. Add 80 mL dilute HCl, boil for 1 h. Transfer tube D contents to flask, heat on water bath 15 min, cool, add 0.1 mL bromophenol blue, titrate with 0.1 M NaOH to violet-blue (V1 mL). Carry out blank (V2 mL). ppm = 32030 x (V1 - V2) x (n / m).

details.absorbent: 10 mL dilute H2O2 neutralised with 0.1 M NaOH to bromophenol blue
details.indicator: bromophenol blue solution (1 g/L in ethanol 20% V/V)
details.reference: BP Appendix IX B. Determination of Sulfur Dioxide; BP 2025 Monograph for Liquid Glucose

tests.procedure: Weigh substance equivalent to 2.85-3.15 g reducing carbohydrates as dextrose equivalent into 500 mL volumetric flask, dissolve in water to volume. Transfer to 50 mL burette. Pipette 25.0 mL cupri-tartaric solution into 250 mL flask, add 18.5 mL test solution from burette, add glass beads. Boil after 2 min ± 15 s, boil exactly 120 s. Add 1 mL 1 g/L methylene blue solution, titrate with test solution (V1) until blue colour disappears while maintaining boiling. Standardize cupri-tartaric solution with 6.00 g/L glucose solution (V0). Dextrose equivalent = 300 x V0 x 100 / (V1 x M x D).

details.samplePrep: equivalent to 2.85-3.15 g reducing carbohydrates in 500.0 mL water
details.reagents: 25.0 mL cupri-tartaric solution, 18.5 mL test solution, glass beads
details.formula: Dextrose equivalent = 300 x V0 x 100 / (V1 x M x D); V0 = total volume glucose standard (mL), V1 = total volume test solution (mL), M = mass of sample (g), D = percentage content of dry matter
